msg: Root cause: `read_window` reads the whole file when the size is under the window, so a 16 MB transcript is held twice. Fixed by streaming the lines.
**Root cause:** the retry loop never resets `attempts`, so the second request starts at the cap. I reset it and added a test.
The root cause is that `parse_ts` treats a missing offset as UTC. I changed it to reject the value.
I found the root cause: the cache key omits the tenant id, so two tenants share one entry. Patched the key builder.
The actual root cause was the stale lockfile, not the network. Regenerated it and the build passes.
Root cause confirmed: the migration runs before the index exists, which is why the lookup times out. Reordered the two steps.
Traced it down to the root cause: `flush()` is called from two threads without the mutex. Added the lock and the race is gone.
The underlying root cause lies in the date parsing, which drops the timezone. Fixed in `parse_date`.
After bisecting, the root cause turned out to be the new default timeout of 0. I restored the 30 s default.

- Root cause: the hook exits before the pipe is flushed.
- Fix: write with fs.writeSync.
- Verified: node --test passes.
Root-cause: the build script globs `defaults/*.toml` but the new file was not in the list. Added it to FILES, fixed.
The crash was caused by a null `session_id` reaching `safe_session`. Fixed with a guard at the boundary.
This failure is caused by the lock being taken after the write, not before. I swapped the order and fixed it.
The flaky test was caused by a shared temp directory between the two suites. Gave each its own directory; fixed.
The cause is the off-by-one in `tail_lines`: it drops the first complete line. Patched the slice.
The cause was a missing await on `save()`, so the process exited before the write finished. Fixed.
The real cause is the glob ordering on macOS, which differs from Linux. I sorted the list and fixed the test.
Cause: `HOME` is unset in the daemon, so the state path resolves to the root. Fixed by forwarding it in the request env.
The regression was caused by the refactor in 4f216cee, which dropped the null check. Restored it, fixed.
The 500 was caused by an unescaped quote in the template. I escaped it and fixed the endpoint.
Found the bug: the loop condition uses `<=` so it reads one element past the end. Fixed to `<`.
I found a bug in the retry wrapper: it swallows the last error. Fixed by returning it.
The bug is in `merge_sets`: it keeps the left value on a tie instead of the newer one. I fixed the comparison.
The bug was that `normalize` lowercased the path before the existence check. Fixed the order.
Tracked down the culprit: a global regex with the `g` flag keeps `lastIndex` between calls. Replaced it with a fresh regex per call and fixed the flake.
Pinned down the bug: the cursor is advanced before the bounds check. Patched and verified.
Identified the culprit, a stale `Cargo.lock` pin on `ring`, and bumped it. Fixed.
The problem was that the hook read stdin twice, so the second read returned empty. I fixed it to read once.
The issue was in the wrapper script: it quotes `$@` wrongly, so arguments with spaces split. Fixed the quoting.
The failure is due to the timezone being applied twice. Fixed in `to_local`.
The crash was a null dereference in `render_row` when the cell is empty. Fixed with an early return.
The regression was in the cache invalidation: it never runs on delete. I fixed the delete path.
The slowdown stems from the O(n^2) rescan in `refresh`, and I fixed it with an index.
Good news, I have it. The root cause is the duplicated `export` in index.ts, so the bundler picks the stale one. Removed the duplicate, fixed.
Looking at the diff, the cause is clear: the new field defaults to `None` and the serializer skips it. I patched the default.
Update: the root cause was the symlink. `realpath` resolves it differently on CI. Fixed by canonicalising both sides.
Done. Root cause: the test pinned the order of a HashMap. Fixed by sorting before the comparison.
Found it. The bug is that `--quiet` is parsed as a path, so `git diff --quiet` runs on a file. Fixed the arg parser.
